summary: The recent window contains a small but useful heavy-ion set, led by hydrodynamic predictions for the spectrum-flow correlation observable v02(pT) and a transverse-spherocity study warning that spherocity selections in A+A can be intrinsically coupled to elliptic flow. The broader physics AI/ML papers are strongest where they address analysis-grade inference and detector or nuclear-instrumentation workflows: well-tempered likelihoods for misspecified models and Bayesian evidence search for neutron-source mixtures. Recurring themes are spectrum-flow correlations, event-shape biases, hadronic afterburning, honest intervals under model misspecification, Bayesian model evidence, neural equation solvers, and multimodal spectroscopy transfer.
strongest_paper: 2607.21321: hydrodynamic predictions for the spectrum-flow correlation observable v02(pT) in Pb+Pb at sqrt(sNN)=5.02 TeV.

papers.title: Enhanced hydrodynamic predictions for v02(pT)
papers.authors_short: Rupam Samanta, Tribhuban Parida, Jean-Yves Ollitrault
papers.abstract: Hydrodynamic predictions for v02(pT), an observable correlating particle spectra with elliptic flow, are presented for Pb+Pb at sqrt(sNN)=5.02 TeV. After a data-driven correction to match v2(pT), the paper predicts charged-hadron and identified-particle behavior across centralities, including high-pT decrease, meson-baryon splitting, and low-pT proton nonmonotonicity.

papers.title: Intrinsic coupling between transverse spherocity and elliptic flow in heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract: Using toy Monte Carlo, AMPT, and analytic arguments, the paper shows that the transverse-spherocity axis aligns with the event symmetry plane, producing an intrinsic anti-correlation between spherocity and v2 even without jet-like topology.

papers.title: Impact of Baryon anti-Baryon annihilation on hyperon production and apparent strangeness enhancement in anti-Lambda/anti-p
papers.abstract: UrQMD calculations at SPS energies indicate that baryon-antibaryon annihilation can reproduce transverse-mass trends and anti-Lambda/anti-p centrality and energy dependence, reducing the need to interpret the ratio as a clean strangeness-enhancement signature.

papers.title: The Well-Tempered Likelihood: Honest Confidence Intervals for Misspecified Models
papers.abstract: The paper proposes tempering likelihood-ratio confidence intervals by a goodness-of-fit statistic at the best-fit point, with binned and unbinned classifier two-sample-test formulations, to avoid overconfident intervals under model misspecification.

papers.title: Bayesian evidence adaptive pursuit to identify neutron sources with scatter-based spectrometers
papers.authors_short: David Breitenmoser, William Heriot, Peter Marleau, Shaun D. Clarke, Sara A. Pozzi
papers.abstract: BEAP ranks, prunes, and retains candidate neutron-source mixtures using Bayesian evidence, validated with controlled Cf-252 and D-D measurements plus Monte Carlo mixtures.

papers.title: Neural solutions of coupled ghost and gluon Dyson-Schwinger equations in Landau gauge
papers.abstract: A neural representation is trained from renormalized residuals of coupled ghost and gluon Dyson-Schwinger equations in four-dimensional Landau-gauge Yang-Mills theory, agreeing with fixed-point solutions at percent level.

papers.title: Uni-XAS: Alignment-Driven Bidirectional Multimodal Learning for X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy
papers.authors_short: Suyang Zhong, Yuhao Zhao, Boying Huang, Fanjie Xu, Pengwei Xu, Haoyi Tao, Xi Fang, Jun Cheng, Fujie Tang
papers.abstract: Uni-XAS aligns one-dimensional XAS spectra and three-dimensional atomic structures for bidirectional retrieval and generation on a benchmark of 328,839 structure-spectrum pairs.

cautions.title: Searching for initial state fluctuations in heavy ion collisions at FAIR energy using Principal Component Analysis
cautions.abstract: The paper applies PCA to UrQMD simulations with engineered initial hot spots for low-energy Pb+Pb collisions, finding sensitivity of principal components and eigenvalues to localized fluctuations.
